errata.text: PROTOCOL section 0 says the seen pre-freeze K = 50 census at k = 16, t = 5 is "re-drawn anyway, with a different seed" at K = 2000. It was not: the first 50 rows of data/census_k16_{v,xeye,even,rand,xAA}_t5.npz reproduce the section 0 table exactly (262.8/255.4, 77.92/278.96, 507.56/259.36, 260.28/256.28, 272.6/266.8), so the seen frames are rows 0-49 of the data cells. The README "smoke and the data run share seeds" list omits this overlap, and the with/without-that-cell verdicts promised in section 0 are not reported. Recomputed by the validator: without those cells P1 44/44, P1x 22/23 (same failing cell), P2 70/70, NC1 11/11, PC2 and NC2 hold; dropping only the 50 rows changes no verdict.
errata.suggested_fix: Leave PROTOCOL.md as frozen. Add an Errata entry to README.md (and REPORT.typ/pdf) stating the overlap, that section 0's "different seed" sentence is wrong, and the with/without verdicts above.

errata.text: P4 total degree: PROTOCOL bounds every f other than x by 2 x its per-variable degree, i.e. 4 for ye. ye measures 6, so ye also fails as frozen. analyse.py uses TOT_MAX ye = 6 (present since c47218b9d5, before the protocol), so it passed ye. The README P-table (and REPORT) say "x 4, v 18, ye 6 and uv 50 were within", and PROTOCOL section 0's smoke disclosure lists xe, q, xeye but not ye, although the smoke also showed ye total degree 6. The P4 total-degree verdict (failed) is unchanged.
errata.suggested_fix: List ye 6 (bound 4) among the P4 total-degree failures and note that analyse.py's TOT_MAX for ye differs from the frozen text.

errata.text: README "What the data show" item 4 (and REPORT): "Per relation, the dense functions cost 1.01-12.3x x on the same [0, 2^t) base". That range covers v and q only (the P6 arms). Over the four dense functions at T = 5 the range is 0.84-12.3: uv at k = 18 is 0.88 and jac6 at k = 20 is 0.84, both below x. At T = 4 it is 0.25-9.8. The noise comes from single-base coverage counts as small as 10 points.
errata.suggested_fix: Restrict the sentence to v and q (P6), or give 0.84-12.3x at T = 5 with the two sub-1 cells and the single-draw caveat.

errata.text: README item 1: "0.989-1.007, in 45/45 qualifying cells". 0.989 is the k = 18 jac6 t = 4 cell, which is not qualifying (mean xm 19.8 < 50). The 45 qualifying cells span 0.993-1.007; all 48 cells span 0.989-1.007.
errata.suggested_fix: Write "0.993-1.007 in the 45 qualifying cells (0.989-1.007 over all 48)".

errata.text: README census paragraph: "argmax-J frame / mean is 1.4-6 at t = 4-7 for both f-frames and x-frames" "in every arm". Over the function arms the f-frames give 1.42-6.03 and the cols-matched x-frames 1.42-7.20. Over all arms, controls included, the f-frames go down to 1.05 and the x-frames to 1.11.
errata.suggested_fix: Give 1.42-6.03 (f-frames) and 1.42-7.20 (x-frames) for the function arms, and say the controls go lower.

errata.text: Outcome label: the README calls the outcome "no verdict: inconclusive, no positive". PROTOCOL section 7 uses "no verdict" only for "Instrument invalid". Here every validity gate passed, the positive rule is not met, and the negative rule fails only because P1x failed. By section 7 the outcome is mixed, reported as it falls.
errata.suggested_fix: Use: "Instrument valid; positive rule not met; negative rule not met (P1x failed in one post-hoc cell); mixed outcome, no positive".

errata.text: Blindness timeline. (a) "Frozen before the smoke test" cannot be verified from git: PROTOCOL.md first appears in 56e5973465 together with the first smoke outputs, and the verifiable freeze b0a6957edb comes after the smoke. The analysis-script predictions do predate any committed smoke output (c47218b9d5). (b) In the draft analysis the P5d threshold was >= 3 at T = 5 (c47218b9d5). It became >= 1.0 at T = 4 and 5 in fcd9e9186a (03:18:24), before the protocol's first commit. The measured 2.12 passes the frozen threshold and would have failed the draft one. The same commit adds runtime instrumentation, which suggests runs were attempted. Section 0 does not mention this, and the record cannot show whether data informed the change.
errata.suggested_fix: Add both points to the README Blindness section and treat P5d as not demonstrably blind.

errata.text: Some result sentences lack their own [pcc:unverified] tag: "P1x failed in one of its 24 cells: x_E.y_E at k = 16, t = 7."; "x refutes at D = 6 at n = 8 and n = 10 on every target." (Answer item 4) and "x refutes at D = 6 at both n = 8 and n = 10." with "the dense functions need D = n at every n" (Power); "Every kernel had dimension 1."; "the x-frames cover 3,264 of 8,209 points there". E[r] has 8,208 non-identity points.
errata.suggested_fix: Tag each sentence, and write 8,208 non-identity points of E[r].

errata.text: macaulay.py's true_decomp double-counts lifts when a Boolean root has value 0, because the lift dictionary stores both P and -P under key 0 = -0. 14 of 933 records show exactly 2x the validator's independent count, all with a zero root value. Census agreement (covered <=> at least one decomposition) is unaffected.
errata.suggested_fix: Note it in the README errata. No rerun is needed.

errata.text: For x, the M2 mul-add proxy is 22.0x (T = 4) and 31.1x (T = 5) the engine F4 count per target (8.91e7 vs 4.05e6; 3.96e9 vs 1.27e8). The README calls the proxy "not the engine's F4 count" but gives no factor, and the "2.12x" dense/x ratio is a ratio between proxies.
errata.suggested_fix: Add the proxy/engine factor for x beside C2 and keep the "2.12x" labelled as a proxy ratio.

errata.text: README Data and .gitignore: "data/*.npz and smoke/*.npz are git-ignored (the 64 KB data-file policy ...)". Every L2 npz is at most 31.3 KB (2.43 MB in total), so the policy did not require excluding them.
